lines.text: Less than a second after liftoff, Challenger was already leaking.
lines.headline:
Already
leaking

lines.text: Smoke was puffing from a joint on the right booster, sealed by two rubber O-rings.
That morning was fifteen degrees colder than any launch before.
And cold rubber springs back slowly.
So when ignition flexed the joint open, the O-rings couldn't keep up, and hot gas blew past them.
Then the smoke stopped, and Challenger flew on.
Fifty-eight seconds in, a flame broke through and swept onto the external fuel tank.
At seventy-three seconds, the tank failed, and Challenger broke apart.
All seven crew members were lost.
The night before, engineers had recommended not launching below fifty-three degrees.
Their managers reversed that advice, and NASA's top launch officials never heard it.
The seal failed in the cold. But the warning failed the night before.
